label: Grid frequency after a 3 GW outage and the three reserves
context: Animate the Continental European grid frequency after the reference incident, the sudden loss of 3,000 MW of generation, and how the reserve products restore it. Top panel: frequency in Hz (y from 49.75 to 50.05) against time (x from -10 s to 15 min, use a broken/log-like axis: first 60 s stretched, then minutes). Bottom panel: stacked power in MW (0 to 3000) supplied by each response against the same time axis. Phase 1 (0-1 s) 'Loss of 3 GW': a red marker; frequency starts falling; label 'inertia of spinning machines slows the fall (rate of change of frequency)'. Phase 2 (1-30 s) 'FCR, frequency containment reserve': frequency nadir about 49.85 Hz then levels at a quasi-steady 49.90 Hz; the FCR area grows to 3,000 MW within 30 s, label 'FCR: shared across Continental Europe, ~3,000 MW, fully active at 200 mHz deviation within 30 s'. Phase 3 (30 s - 5 min) 'aFRR, automatic frequency restoration reserve': the control area's controller ramps aFRR up while FCR ramps down; frequency climbs back to 50.00 Hz; label 'aFRR: activated by the TSO's controller, full within 5 min'. Phase 4 (5-15 min) 'mFRR, manual frequency restoration reserve': mFRR replaces aFRR, which is freed for the next event; label 'mFRR: full within 12.5 min'. Phase 5: caption 'After that, the balancing group responsible pays the imbalance price.' Colours: frequency line #04204B, FCR #0B4FC0, aFRR #138374, mFRR #B4552F, outage marker #B4552F. Text >= 12 px, white background, loop every ~24 s.

spec.title: Grid frequency after a 3 GW outage and the three reserves
spec.caption: After the loss of 3,000 MW, FCR arrests the frequency fall within 30 s. aFRR then restores 50.00 Hz and frees FCR. mFRR takes over from aFRR within 12.5 min. After that, the balancing group responsible pays the imbalance price.
